recordings.name: kepler_ellipse
recordings.title: Kepler orbit, e = 0.6
recordings.caption: One planet round a heavy sun, CVODE Adams, 360 frames of dt = 0.02 (t = 7.2, about two orbits). Watch the speed swing between perihelion and aphelion. Measured over the recording: |dE|/E = 9.8e-8, |dL|/|L| = 1.3e-7.

recordings.name: tumbling_racket
recordings.title: The tennis-racket theorem
recordings.caption: A torque-free cuboid (half-extents 1.6, 0.9, 0.25) spun about its INTERMEDIATE principal axis. It flips end over end — the Dzhanibekov effect — while the angular momentum stays put: measured |d|L||/|L| = 0 exactly, |dE|/E = 6.4e-9 over t = 4.

recordings.name: box_of_shapes
recordings.title: Mixed shapes in a rigid box
recordings.caption: The regression scenario mixed_shapes_rattle_in_the_box_conserving_energy: a cylinder, a disk and a cuboid inside a rigid BOX 4 whose six wall slabs have inverse_mass = 0, with G = 0. 36 real CVODE rootfinding events in t = 3; measured |dE|/E = 3.4e-16, i.e. exact to the last bit. Gold arrows are the analytic contact normals, scaled by the applied impulse. |L| about the origin is NOT conserved here, and should not be: the immovable walls supply outside torque.

recordings.name: double_pendulum_hinges
recordings.title: Double pendulum on two hinges
recordings.caption: Two HINGE joints — each fixing a point and an axis, each leaving one freedom — assembled into the classic chaotic linkage. 400 frames of dt = 0.01 (t = 4), every one a real IDA step on the constrained DAE. The gold rings are the joints; their axes run along z, straight at you in this opening view, so drag to see them. Measured: the joints hold to |g| = 5.6e-8 over the whole recording. Energy wanders by 4.5e-3 against a scale of mgL = 14.7 — 3 parts in 10,000 — and the same mechanism run as ONE continuous 4 s integration instead of 400 separate steps holds it to 7.4e-5, because each step restarts the multistep solver at order one.

recordings.name: universal_joint
recordings.title: A universal joint transmitting rotation
recordings.caption: A torque spins the input shaft up from rest; the Cardan joint carries the rotation across to the output shaft, which a rod braces to a post. The bend runs from straight to cos-inverse 0.6 = 53.130 degrees and back, and the speed ratio across the joint swings with it — a Cardan joint is not a constant-velocity joint.

recordings.name: ball_joint_chain
recordings.title: A chain on ball joints
recordings.caption: Four links hung on BALL joints. A ball joint holds one point and frees all three rotations, so unlike the hinged double pendulum this chain is not trapped in a plane. The start is a rigid rotation of the whole assembly about the vertical at 1.5 rad/s, which satisfies every joint exactly, so the run begins on the constraint manifold: |g| = 0 and |g_dot| = 0, both exactly, with no consistent-velocity projection. Give the identical start to the same chain built from HINGE joints and |g_dot| = 1.5 -- exactly the whirl rate, because the whirl is the one thing a hinge forbids. Watch the z axis: every link starts exactly on the plane z = 0 and the chain reaches |z| = 1.7147, where a hinge chain would still be at exactly zero. Measured over this recording: the four joints hold to |g| = 3.3e-9, and |dE|/E = 2.8e-4 across 250 separate IDA restarts, one per frame.

recordings.name: rod_pendulum_chain
recordings.title: Four bobs on four rods
recordings.caption: A CONSTRAIN is the smallest joint there is: one row, holding one scalar fact, g = |d| - L. Four rods on four free bobs is 4 rows on 24 freedoms, against 3 rows per BALL, 4 per UNIVERSAL and 5 per HINGE. It is also the best conditioned joint -- one well-scaled scalar equation, with none of the index-2 orientation coupling that forces a tolerance floor on the other three -- so run this chain as ONE integration at the default 1e-10/1e-12 and the rods hold to |g| = 5.4e-15, which is roundoff. This recording is not one integration, though. It is 250 cold restarts, one per frame, and the tolerance a continuous run sustains is not the tolerance a restart sustains: at the default these same four rods fail on the SECOND restart. So the scene asks for 1e-6/1e-8 by hand -- exactly the floor an orientation joint gets automatically and never has to request. Measured over this recording: the four rods hold to |g| = 7.8e-8. Released from rest, so the start is on the constraint manifold with nothing to project.

recordings.name: spinning_top
recordings.title: A spinning top, precessing
recordings.caption: A top held at its tip by a BALL joint -- one point held, all three rotations free, which is exactly what the tip of a top is. A symmetric top spinning at w3 about its own axis, its centre of mass a distance r from the pivot, precesses at Omega = Mgr/(I3 w3). That is usually the fast-top APPROXIMATION, but this top is mounted with its axis horizontal, and at 90 degrees the correction term carries a cos(theta) that is exactly zero -- so the formula is exact here. With M = 1, r = 0.6, g = 3 and I3 = 0.0882, spinning at 20 rad/s, it predicts 1.0204081632653061 rad/s and a period of 6.1575 s. Measured over this recording: 1.020440 rad/s, three parts in 100,000, with the axis staying horizontal to 4.3e-5 -- it does not nutate at all, because it was started ON the steady solution, which takes the precession velocity as well as the spin. Released with only its spin it misses the formula by 7.8%. The joint holds to |g| = 4.3e-7.

recordings.name: gyroscope_gimbal
recordings.title: A gyroscope in a gimbal
recordings.caption: Three HINGE joints on three mutually perpendicular axes: 15 rows on 18 freedoms, leaving exactly the three gimbal angles. Every body is concentric, so all three hinge axes pass through one point -- the rings only LOOK nested, and no centre moves further from the origin than 7e-35. Unlike the spinning top, gravity does nothing here: there the centre of mass hung a distance r from the pivot and weight had a lever arm, while here every centre of mass sits ON the pivot, so the arm is zero. A hinge transmits no torque about its own axis, which gives two exact invariants: nothing can torque the system about the vertical, so total L.y = 0.6314 is held to 6.4e-15; and the innermost hinge IS the rotor's spin axis, so its axial spin I3 w3 = 3.75 is held to 1 part in 100,000. Watch what the gyroscope does with the push: the whole assembly is started turning about the vertical at 1 rad/s, yet the outer ring never gets more than 11.15 degrees from where it began -- the rotation comes back out as a TILT, the rotor's axis swinging up to 20.06 degrees away at right angles to the push. The three joints hold to |g| = 3.5e-8.
